messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-prod-gpu-12' p99 latency breach detected (SLO: 3s). auto-escalation to on-call. @maya is oncall.
maya: acked. seeing alerts for p95 ~ 320ms and p99 ~ 5.1s at the moment, streaming stalls showing timeouts at ~10s. queue depth jumped to 430. taking. :rotating_light:
maya: quick check — dashboard shows pool GPU utl ~= 97%, warmup completions lagging (avg warmup 12s), autoscaler reported scale request at +00:01:30 but new nodes not ready.
alex: adding context — autoscaler logs show long provisioning latencies in region (cloud provider API throttling) + instance warmup not hitting prewarm image; many pods in CrashLoopBackOff for init scripts.
jordan: runtime traces show KV cache miss rate spiked 3x, incremental latency per token. streaming stalls correlate with large batch sizes hitting warmup boundary.
maya: possible customer impact? evan can you confirm if any high-tier customers saw errors?
evan: ACME-Prod errored on long streaming sessions, CS reported increased retries for their realtime summarizer. Marking "high user impact" for now. Notified account owner.
lia: digging into pool allocation: reserved capacity hit 100% for dedicated-12, fallback policy attempted region failover but routing policy locked to eu-west-2. Requests queued instead of falling back to hosted variants.
alex: command run: ```
# check pods in pool
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=dedicated-12 -o wide
# autoscaler events
kubectl -n infra get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler
```
maya: observed autoscaler event: `ScaleUp: waiting for nodes (cloud API rate limit)`. Scaling delay ~ 90s.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: noticed a deploy 8m ago to runtime-init that changed init-image tag (v1.4.9 -> v1.5.0). Rolling-restart triggered.
jordan: that deploy may explain CrashLoopBackOffs during warmup. v1.5.0 introduced a new init check that delays readiness on heavy models.
maya: mitigation plan (live): 1) reduce incoming concurrency per-queue for this pool to lower queueing and tail latency. 2) enable manual burst-capacity (reserve hot nodes) if cloud permits. 3) route non-SLA traffic to hosted-api in another region. 4) rollback runtime-init deploy if warmup fails continue.
alex: executed temporary throttling: `infra rate-limit set pool=dedi-12 max-inflight=120` — reduced inflight from 320 to 120. seeing immediate drop in p99 to ~3.6s.
lia: I can trigger manual pool scale if ops approves. cloud quota available for +4 instances in region.
maya: please do manual scale now, jordan stay on rollback path.
lia: manual scale request sent to cloud: instance-type g4dn.xlarge +4. Cloud accepted, provisioning started.
jordan: preparing rollback: `kubectl -n infra set image daemon/runtime-init=registry.redwood/v1.4.9` ready if warmup doesn't improve in 3m.
maya: observed customer impact: ACME had 11% error rate on streaming endpoints between 1718499900 and 1718500200. Need post-incident follow up with CS. evan please coordinate.
evan: on it — pinged ACME PM and CS lead. Tentatively scheduling 30m sync after stabilization.
ops-bot: cloud-notify: 2 of 4 new instances reached RUNNING after 85s; kube nodes registered.
lia: new nodes joined, kube DaemonSets scheduled. Warmup tasks starting. average warmup time dropping to 6s. queue depth falling to 140.
maya: p95 now 180ms, p99 down to 2.4s. streaming stalls <3 reported. still watching for residual errors.
alex: running quick smoke: sample streaming workload shows end-to-end 600 token session completed with steady token throughput. logs show fewer KV cache misses.
jordan: toggled temporary routing rule: allow fallback to hosted-small-quantized for requests >5s queue wait. should reduce customer-visible stalls for non-critical sessions.
maya: rollback not executed. deploy owner to follow up on init-image issue in postmortem.
evan: ACME confirmed latency improved and retries dropped after 1718500300, will keep them updated.
maya: incident level -> SEV2. We'll keep monitoring 30m. start a short incident bridge? might be useful to coordinate followups.
alex: suggested runbook items for postmortem: - root cause: deploy changed init behavior + cloud provisioning latency + routing policy prevented fallback. - why autoscaler didn't mitigate: provider throttling + no prewarmed nodes. - customer impact timeline. - mitigation: add prewarm pool, lower default max-inflight, decouple routing lock for critical failover.
lia: creating follow-up tickets: INFRA-4235 (prewarm pool), RUNTIME-781 (revert/init-fix), ROUTING-112 (enable emergency-fallback).
maya: handoff: I'm staying for 15 more minutes to ensure stability, then handing to alex for overnight watch. alex you good to take the rest?
alex: taking on watch. will keep the bridge open for 30m and run postmortem draft.
maya: thanks. final checks — p99 2.1s, queue depth 60, GPU util 72%. closing active mitigation. logging incident in incidents tracker.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SEV2 -> mitigated. Please file postmortem by 1718560000.
maya: filing quick notes into the runbook now. evan, please attach customer timeline to the postmortem.
evan: will attach CS timeline and support tickets. also flag ACME for follow-up call.
alex: action items captured. postmortem owner: alex. next steps: root cause analysis, deploy gating for init-image changes, add autoscaler runbook for cloud backoff scenarios.
maya: thanks team. :thumbsup:"
